lore_anchors.definition: A post-Tribulation power that surpasses Divine Sense; allows a Celestial Immortal to vaguely touch upon fate.
The periodic ordeals faced by cultivators before the Heavenly Tribulation; minor disasters every three hundred years, major calamities every nine hundred.
A top-ten divine ability since Pangu; allows the user’s hands to rival magic treasures in power.
A Loose Immortal and senior disciple-brother of the Diancai Immortal from the Black-White College.
The central marketplace of a commandery city, where cultivators buy and sell treasures.
A soul-binding vow enforced by the cosmos itself; breaking it results in instant soul annihilation.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why didn’t Ji Ning tell his servants about Yuchi Xiyue?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He learned that the Yuchi clan’s secrets were pried out by soul-scrying—even absolute loyalty can be bypassed by a powerful enough enemy.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What is Heartforce and how is it different from Divine Sense?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Heartforce is a post-Tribulation power that comes after the soul and Primal fully merge; it is more powerful and can even sense fate, whereas Divine Sense is limited to perception and telekinesis.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Is the Starseizing Hand’s second cycle a big deal?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Yes—it makes Ji Ning’s hands as strong as Immortal-ranked treasures; before this, they were far weaker.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why is the Black-White College giving Ji Ning secret manuals for free?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Because the Diancai Immortal requested it before leaving, and the college views Ji Ning’s upcoming Immortal Fortunes Assembly and his conflict with the Shaoyin clan as serious enough to bypass normal rules.
A Primal Daoist assassin bound by a Heavenly Dao oath to kill Ji Ning within three days; he is currently stuck waiting outside the Yan Prince’s manor.
